questions.q: Does every business's fiscal year have to run January through December?
options: Yes, this is a legal requirement everywhere
Yes, because accounting software cannot support other configurations
No fiscal year can ever be shorter or longer than exactly 12 months
No — a business can define its fiscal year differently, for example February through January, as long as it consistently uses that calendar
questions.explain: Many businesses use a calendar fiscal year, but others (like some retailers) choose a different 12-month cycle to better match their business cycle.

questions.q: What does a fiscal calendar define?
options: The exact dollar amounts a business expects to earn
Which dates belong to which accounting period
The names of every account in the chart of accounts
A business's tax rate for the year
questions.explain: A fiscal calendar maps specific dates to specific reporting periods (period 1, period 2, etc.), which the accounting system then uses consistently.

questions.q: What does 'closing a period' operationally mean?
options: Deleting all of that period's transactions
Automatically reopening the period after 30 days
Locking the period so no further transactions can be posted into it, once its accounting work is complete
Converting the period from accrual to cash accounting
questions.explain: Closing a period locks it against new postings to protect the integrity of financial statements that have already been reported on.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'closed' period and a 'permanently closed' period?
options: A closed period can potentially be reopened for a genuine correction; a permanently closed period is locked for good
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A permanently closed period can still accept new transactions
A closed period has never had any transactions posted to it
questions.explain: Closed periods can sometimes be reopened if truly needed, while permanently closed periods are locked with no realistic expectation of reopening.

questions.q: What is a common real-world support issue that traces back to period status, according to this lesson?
options: A user asking why a report shows the wrong currency
A user asking why their password expired
A user asking how to change their email address
A user asking why they cannot post a transaction, which often traces back to that period being closed
questions.explain: A large category of 'why can't I post this' support tickets traces back to the relevant accounting period being closed.
